clips.text: I did 15 workouts. I worked out for a lot of teams. Coming out of college, I didn't average a lot of minutes and I didn't average a lot of points at UCLA, so a lot of people were doubting my offensive prowess and my offensive contributions. This was the first time this had ever happened to me because coming up, it was just disrespect to somebody think they can score on you. So I was always going to play defense on a respect tip. But I was never looked at as no defender. I was looked at as somebody who going to do everything, who going to get you 30, who going to lock up, who going to get a few blocks. So it was never no thing to me that I was thinking about. But at UCLA, I played really, really good defense and my defensive film was amazing. clips.speaker: Peyton Watson
clips.team: Cousins with Vince Carter & Tracy McGrady
clips.text: We knew pretty right away that the pick was going to get traded after I got drafted, but it was still one of those things where you envision something in your head. It's like you open a present on Christmas, but then you like, oh, that's for your brother instead. You like, oh, I thought I was going to get that. But at the end of the day, I'm still getting a present, so I'm cool. It was one of those things for me where I felt blessed to be there no matter what. Obviously, the Thunder are a great organization and they've built into being one of the best organizations in the league. Hats off to them. And then that next year with the Nuggets I won a championship. So there was no bad place for me. That was really God looking over me and telling me that this is his plan and it's going to work out for me.
clips.news_angle: Peyton Watson describes his draft night trade experience
clips.social_post: Peyton Watson compares his draft night trade to opening a Christmas present only to realize it was meant for your brother. He says he felt blessed regardless and ended up winning a championship with the Nuggets the following year.

clips.speaker: Peyton Watson
clips.team: Cousins with Vince Carter & Tracy McGrady
clips.text: What was a shock to me was first of all it being a players' league, so that meaning I was used to my coach really getting on us. I'm talking about we doing everything right and it ain't no attitudes, nobody looking sideways, body language in check, everything like that. But coming into the league and being with guys who make ten times what the coach make, it was just a complete whirlwind for me because the players take a lot of the ownership. They take a lot of the blame when you lose, they take a lot of the credit when you win, and the coaches they do get on you and they hold you accountable, but it's not the same that I was used to growing up. So that was one thing that I was shocked at. And then the other thing that I was shocked at was how detailed certain guys' routines were.

clips.social_post: Peyton Watson says the biggest shock of entering the NBA was realizing it is a players league where stars hold the power and accountability compared to the coach-led environments he was used to growing up.
